tighn_host.text: Tigh Neachtain is Irish for 'Naughton's house'. It is a Cross Street landmark, with a very good fire.
Cross Street is in the old medieval core of Galway, a few steps from the Spanish Arch and the quays.
Galway had Fourteen Tribes, merchant families: Athy, Blake, Bodkin, Browne, D'Arcy, Deane, Font, French, Joyce, Kirwan, Lynch, Martin, Morris, Skerrett.

tighn_piper.text: The uilleann pipes are played with a bellows under the elbow, not blown into. Uilleann means 'of the elbow'.
It takes about seven years to get a decent tune out of them. The neighbours take a bit longer to forgive you.

galway_quizmaster.text: Quiz night at Tigh Neachtain! Please keep the singing to the gaps between questions. Looking at you, third table.
Five questions. I'm the quizmaster, so I'm always right, and I have the laminated answers to prove it.
Fancy a round? Five questions, no phones.

else.text: Fair enough. The fire's lovely, anyway.
